title: A prime over a principal ideal in a local normalization contains a height-one prime over it
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where an integral domain is a nonzero commutative ring without zero divisors. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ be its field of fractions and $N\subseteq K$ its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Assume $R$ is local, meaning it has a unique maximal ideal. For every $0\ne b\in N$ and every prime ideal $P\subset N$ containing $b$, there exists a height-one prime ideal $Q\subseteq P$ of $N$ containing $b$. Here a height-one prime is a nonzero prime with no prime strictly between it and $(0)$. No Noetherianity hypothesis on $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Swanson–Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules. Theorem 4.10.5 proof, printed p. 91 (PDF p. 105), paragraph beginning We next prove that for any non-zero element b: the principal-height refinement subclaim, proved using Lemma 4.8.4, contraction of integral closures of principal ideals, and the Dimension Inequality B.2.5. It precedes and does not assume the final height-one intersection assertion. Author-hosted PDF read online at https://www.math.purdue.edu/~iswanso/book/SwansonHuneke.pdf; local PDF WANTED.
